lesson.intro:
Welcome to the machine. Before you ever indicate to pull out of a parking space on Oranienstraße, Germany wants to know three things about you: **what** you are allowed to drive, **whether you are fit** to drive it, and **how much rope** you get before the state quietly takes your licence back. That is what this first module is about — the rules that apply to *you*, the driver, rather than to the road.

German driving law is refreshingly unromantic here. It uses numbers: 3,500 kg, two years, 0.0 promille, eight points. Learn these numbers now and the rest of the course becomes far less frightening, because the theory exam (die theoretische Prüfung) loves them, and because the consequences of getting them wrong are expensive in a very German, very well-documented way.

sections.heading: What a class B licence actually buys you
sections.body:
Class B (Klasse B) is the ordinary car licence, and it is defined by mass rather than by how the vehicle looks. You may drive motor vehicles with a maximum authorised mass (zulässige Gesamtmasse) of **no more than 3,500 kg**, designed to carry **no more than eight passengers besides the driver** — so nine seats in total, including yours. A big VW Bus with nine seats: fine. A 4-tonne motorhome: not fine.

Trailers (Anhänger) have their own logic. On plain class B you may pull:

- a trailer with a maximum authorised mass of **up to 750 kg**, full stop; or
- a heavier trailer, **provided the whole combination stays within 3,500 kg**.

Two extras exist for people who need more. Key number **B96** (Schlüsselzahl 96) is not a new class — it is a seven-hour training course noted in your licence that lifts the combination limit to **4,250 kg**. Class **BE** is a real class with its own test and allows a trailer of up to **3,500 kg**. And key number **B196** lets you ride 125 cc / 11 kW motorcycles in Germany only, if you are at least **25** and have held class B for at least **five years**.

Finally, class B comes with two freebies included: **AM** (mopeds and small scooters up to 45 km/h) and **L** (agricultural and forestry tractors up to 40 km/h). What it does *not* include is A1 — the 125 cc motorbike your flatmate keeps offering you.

callout.text: Exam trap: the 3,500 kg figure is the *maximum authorised mass* (what the vehicle may weigh fully loaded), not what it weighs empty. Check the vehicle registration document (Fahrzeugschein), not your intuition.

sections.heading: The paperwork marathon before the fun starts

callout.text: Two wrong 5-point questions = failed exam. Treat every 5-point question in this app as a mini-exam of its own.

sections.heading: Probezeit: two years on trial
sections.body:
Your first ever licence is issued **on probation** (auf Probe). The probationary period (Probezeit) lasts **two years** from the day it is issued, and it applies to first-time licence holders only — classes AM, L and T are exempt from it. If you came via accompanied driving at 17, the clock starts then, so your Probezeit typically ends around your 19th birthday.

Probezeit does not mean special leniency and it does not mean a special speed limit. You get points in Flensburg exactly like everyone else. What changes is that violations are additionally sorted into two baskets:

- **A-violations** (schwerwiegende Zuwiderhandlungen) — serious ones: exceeding a speed limit by 21 km/h or more, jumping a red light, mobile phone at the wheel, tailgating, any drink- or drug-driving offence, driving without your BF17 companion.
- **B-violations** (weniger schwerwiegende Zuwiderhandlungen) — lesser ones: bald tyres, an overdue vehicle inspection (Hauptuntersuchung), children not properly secured.

The escalation is a staircase, and it is automatic — no official has discretion to be nice:

- **One A-violation, or two B-violations** → you are ordered to attend an **Aufbauseminar** (a paid remedial course at a driving school) **and** your Probezeit is extended by two years, making four in total.
- **Another A-violation (or two more B-violations) after the seminar** → a written warning (Verwarnung) plus a recommendation to take traffic-psychology counselling (verkehrspsychologische Beratung) within two months.
- **Another one after that** → the licence is withdrawn (Entziehung der Fahrerlaubnis). You may reapply at the earliest **three months** later.

And if you simply ignore the order to attend the Aufbauseminar? The authority *must* withdraw your licence. Ignoring German post is never the winning move.

callout.text: One single serious mistake — one red light on Frankfurter Allee — is enough to trigger a seminar and add two years to your Probezeit. There is no free first strike for A-violations.

sections.heading: Alcohol, cannabis and the chemistry of losing your licence
sections.body:
Germany runs several alcohol thresholds at once, and the exam expects you to know which is which.

- **0.5 promille** blood alcohol (0.25 mg/l breath) — the general limit. Reach it and you commit an administrative offence (Ordnungswidrigkeit): for a first offence **500 euros, 2 points and a one-month driving ban** (Fahrverbot).
- **0.3 promille** — from here you can already be *prosecuted* if alcohol shows in your driving: weaving, an accident, a stupid manoeuvre. Lawyers call it relative unfitness (relative Fahruntüchtigkeit).
- **1.1 promille** — absolute unfitness (absolute Fahruntüchtigkeit). This is a **criminal offence** (Straftat) even if you drove immaculately: fine or prison, 3 points, licence gone.
- **1.6 promille** — from here the authority orders a medical-psychological examination (**MPU**, medizinisch-psychologische Untersuchung) before you may ever drive again. The same threshold applies to **cyclists**: 1.6 promille on a bike is a criminal offence, and it can cost you your car licence even though no engine was involved.
- **0.0 promille** — for everyone **in the Probezeit** and everyone **under 21**, whichever applies. No beer, no Radler, no "but it was only one". Penalty: **250 euros and 1 point** — plus it counts as an A-violation, so the Aufbauseminar follows automatically.

Cannabis got its own number in 2024: **3.5 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood serum** is the general limit, punished like alcohol (500 euros, 2 points, one month ban; 1,000 euros if you have also been drinking). For novice drivers in the Probezeit and everyone under 21 the same **zero rule** applies to THC as to alcohol — the only exception being THC from a medicine prescribed for you and taken as directed.

Other drugs — cocaine, amphetamine, methamphetamine, MDMA, heroin, morphine — are pure zero tolerance: **detection in your blood is enough**. And prescription medicines are not automatically harmless. Antihistamines, strong painkillers, sedatives and cough syrups can all make you unfit to drive; read the leaflet, ask the pharmacist, and remember that being medically prescribed something is no defence if you can no longer drive safely.

callout.text: Alcohol takes roughly one hour per 0.1–0.15 promille to leave your body, and nothing speeds it up — not coffee, not a shower, not a döner. After a heavy Friday night you can still be over the limit on Saturday morning.

sections.heading: Points in Flensburg, explained without the myths
sections.body:
Every driver in Germany has a file in the driver fitness register (Fahreignungsregister) in the town of Flensburg. A single violation is worth **one, two or three points**:

- **1 point** — an ordinary offence affecting road safety (e.g. moderate speeding).
- **2 points** — a particularly serious offence, typically one that also brings a driving ban, or a traffic crime without licence withdrawal.
- **3 points** — a traffic crime (Straftat) in which the court withdraws the licence or imposes an isolated bar on re-applying (Sperre). A driving ban handed down alongside a conviction is not enough for 3 points; that case stays at 2.

The consequences arrive on a fixed ladder: at **4–5 points** a written admonition (Ermahnung); at **6–7 points** a written warning (Verwarnung); at **8 points** the authority **must** withdraw your licence. After that you may apply again at the earliest **six months** later, and normally only with a positive **MPU** report in your hand.

Two useful details. A voluntary driver fitness seminar (Fahreignungsseminar) removes **one point** — but only while you are on 1 to 5 points, and only once every five years. And points expire by themselves: 1-point entries after **two years and six months**, 2-point entries after **five years**, 3-point entries after **ten years**. Each entry ages individually; there is no single "my points reset" date.

callout.text: 8 points = licence withdrawn. Not "maybe", not "a hearing" — the law says the authority has to do it.

sections.heading: Fitness to drive: the part no test can measure for you
sections.body:
The law expects you to be *able* to drive, not merely licensed to. Three everyday killers rarely feel like offences at the time.

**Tiredness.** Microsleep (Sekundenschlaf) arrives unannounced and lasts a few seconds — at 90 km/h you cover 25 metres every second with your eyes effectively shut. Cold air, loud music and coffee buy you minutes, not hours. The only real fix is to stop and take a nap of **15 to 20 minutes**. On a long trip, plan a break roughly every two hours.

**Emotions.** Rage after an argument, grief, exam panic or the euphoria of a promotion all narrow your attention and push you towards risk. If your hands are shaking on the steering wheel, the tram going past is not your real problem. Wait, walk, breathe, then drive.

**Eyes, ears and health.** Wear the glasses noted in your licence. Get your eyes rechecked as the years pass — no one tells you to. And if illness, a new medication or a fresh injury means you cannot control the car safely, you must not drive: continuing anyway and endangering others is a criminal offence, not bad luck.

Berlin adds its own flavour to all of this: trams on the left, cyclists on the right, delivery vans double-parked in front of you and tourists stepping off kerbs without looking. All of that demands a fully awake, sober, unflustered brain — which is exactly what the rules in this module are protecting.

callout.text: Driving while too tired to react is not a grey area. If you cause an accident because you fell asleep, courts treat it as your decision to drive, not an accident that happened to you.

key_takeaways: Class B: up to 3,500 kg, max 8 passengers plus you, and it includes AM and L for free.
Trailer on plain B: up to 750 kg, or heavier if the whole combination stays under 3,500 kg (B96 lifts it to 4,250 kg, BE to a 3,500 kg trailer).
Probezeit lasts 2 years; one A-violation or two B-violations means Aufbauseminar plus 2 extra years.
0.5 promille is the general limit; 1.1 promille is a crime; 1.6 promille triggers an MPU — and 1.6 on a bicycle counts too.
In the Probezeit and under 21: 0.0 for alcohol and 0.0 for THC. 250 euros, 1 point, and it's an A-violation.
Drugs are zero tolerance; cannabis has a 3.5 ng/ml THC limit for everyone else; medicines can also make you unfit.
Violations cost 1–3 points; 4–5 Ermahnung, 6–7 Verwarnung, 8 points and the licence is gone for at least 6 months.
Microsleep is unstoppable by coffee — the only cure is stopping for 15–20 minutes.

german_terms.en: the legal entitlement to drive (the licence as a right)
probationary period (2 years for new drivers)
per mille — the unit for blood alcohol concentration
unfitness to drive (through alcohol or drugs)
temporary driving ban (you keep the licence, you just may not drive)
driver fitness register — the 'points in Flensburg'

questions.text: What are you allowed to drive on a plain class B licence, without any additional key numbers?

options.text: Motor vehicles with a maximum authorised mass of up to 3,500 kg, built to carry no more than eight passengers besides the driver
A motorcycle with 125 cc and 11 kW, immediately and without any extra training or entry in the licence
A lorry with a maximum authorised mass of 7.5 tonnes

questions.explanation: Class B is defined by mass and seats: no more than 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass, and no more than eight passenger seats plus the driver's (nine in total). Anything heavier needs C1 or C. A 125 cc motorcycle needs class A1 — or key number B196, which requires you to be at least 25, to have held class B for five years, and to complete a training course.

questions.text: Which trailers may you tow on a plain class B licence?

options.text: A trailer with a maximum authorised mass of up to 750 kg
A heavier trailer, provided the maximum authorised mass of the whole combination does not exceed 3,500 kg
Any trailer at all, as long as the towing car itself stays below 3,500 kg

questions.explanation: Two options exist on class B: a small trailer up to 750 kg regardless of the car, or a bigger trailer as long as car plus trailer together stay within 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass. The car's own weight is never the only thing that counts. If you need more, key number B96 raises the combination limit to 4,250 kg after a seven-hour course, and class BE (a separate test) allows a trailer of up to 3,500 kg.

questions.text: Which licence classes are automatically included in class B?

options.text: Class AM — mopeds and small scooters up to 45 km/h
Class L — agricultural and forestry tractors up to 40 km/h
Class A1 — motorcycles up to 125 cc, included automatically

questions.explanation: Class B includes AM and L at no extra cost, which is why a class B holder may legally ride a 45 km/h scooter through Berlin. A1 is not included: 125 cc machines need either class A1 or the German-only key number B196, which has its own age and experience conditions.

questions.text: Which statements about the probationary period (Probezeit) are correct?

options.text: It lasts two years and starts on the day your first driving licence is issued
Violations during the Probezeit also earn points in the Fahreignungsregister in the normal way
During the Probezeit you are not allowed to drive on the Autobahn

questions.explanation: The Probezeit runs for two years from the issue of your first licence (for accompanied driving at 17, from the issue of the provisional certificate, so it usually ends around your 19th birthday). It is an extra layer of consequences, not a separate rulebook: points, fines and driving bans apply exactly as they do to everybody else, and there is no Autobahn ban and no special speed limit for novice drivers in Germany.

questions.text: You commit one serious violation (A-Verstoß) during your two-year Probezeit. What follows?

options.text: The authority orders you to attend an Aufbauseminar at your own expense
Your Probezeit is extended by two years, making four years in total
Nothing happens yet — action is only taken after a second serious violation

questions.explanation: One A-violation, or two B-violations, is enough: the remedial seminar is ordered and the Probezeit is automatically extended by two years. Officials have no discretion here. If you ignore the order and do not attend within the deadline, your licence must be withdrawn. A further A-violation after the seminar brings a written warning plus a recommendation of traffic-psychology counselling; one more after that and the licence is withdrawn, with a three-month minimum wait before you can reapply.

questions.text: You are 19 years old and in your Probezeit. Which statements about alcohol and cannabis are correct?

options.text: You must not drive after consuming any alcohol at all — your limit is 0.0
The same zero rule applies to cannabis (THC), unless the THC comes from a medicine prescribed for you and taken as directed
Because you are over 18, the general 0.5 promille limit applies to you as well

questions.explanation: A strict ban on alcohol and on THC applies to every driver in the Probezeit and to every driver under 21 — so at 19 and on probation you are covered twice over. Breaching it costs 250 euros and 1 point, and because drink- and drug-driving count as a serious A-violation, an Aufbauseminar plus a two-year extension of the Probezeit follows automatically. The only exception is THC from a medicine that was prescribed for you for a specific condition and taken as directed.

questions.text: Which statements about blood alcohol limits for car drivers are correct?

options.text: The general limit is 0.5 promille; reaching it is an administrative offence with a fine, points and normally a one-month driving ban
From 1.1 promille you count as absolutely unfit to drive and commit a criminal offence, even if you made no driving mistake at all
As long as you stay below 1.1 promille, driving after drinking can never be a criminal offence

questions.explanation: 0.5 promille (0.25 mg/l breath) is the general threshold: a first offence typically means 500 euros, 2 points and a one-month driving ban. From 1.1 promille the law assumes absolute unfitness to drive, which is a criminal offence regardless of how well you drove. And the third option is the classic trap: from as little as 0.3 promille you can be prosecuted if alcohol-related driving errors or an accident show that you were unfit — so there is no safe zone below 1.1.

questions.text: Which statements about accompanied driving from 17 (begleitetes Fahren ab 17, BF17) are correct?

options.text: The accompanying person must be at least 30 years old and must have held a class B licence for at least five years
When the licence is applied for, the accompanying person must not have more than one point in the Fahreignungsregister
You may make short trips on your own, as long as your accompanying person has agreed to it

questions.explanation: BF17 lets you drive from 17, but only with a person named in your papers who is at least 30, has held class B for at least five years, and had no more than one point in the register when the application was made. That person must also be sober — at 0.25 mg/l breath alcohol or more, or 3.5 ng/ml THC or more, they may not accompany you. Driving without your named companion is a serious A-violation, so it triggers an Aufbauseminar and extends your Probezeit.

questions.text: You cycle home from a bar in Kreuzberg after a long evening. Which statements are correct?

options.text: From 1.6 promille you count as absolutely unfit to ride and commit a criminal offence
The licensing authority can order an MPU afterwards and can withdraw your car licence, even though you were only on a bicycle
Cyclists commit an administrative offence from 0.5 promille, exactly as car drivers do

questions.explanation: The 0.5 promille administrative offence applies to motor vehicles, so it does not catch cyclists — but the criminal offence of driving while intoxicated covers all vehicles, and for cyclists the courts assume absolute unfitness from 1.6 promille. From that level the licensing authority must order a medical-psychological assessment (MPU) to check your fitness to drive, and a negative result can cost you your car licence, even if you have never driven drunk. Below 1.6 you can also be prosecuted if you weave, fall or cause an accident from about 0.3 promille.

questions.text: Which statements about drugs and medicines behind the wheel are correct?

options.text: For cannabis, a limit of 3.5 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood serum applies to drivers in general
If cocaine, amphetamine or heroin is detected in your blood, that alone is enough for an administrative offence with a fine, points and a driving ban
Medicines prescribed by a doctor can never impair your fitness to drive, so there is no need to read the leaflet

questions.explanation: Since August 2024 cannabis has a statutory limit of 3.5 ng/ml THC in blood serum for drivers generally — a first offence costs 500 euros, 2 points and a one-month ban, rising to 1,000 euros if alcohol is involved as well. Novice drivers in the Probezeit and everyone under 21 have no allowance at all. For the other listed drugs, mere detection in your blood is enough; there is no tolerated quantity. Medication is not harmless either: sedatives, strong painkillers, some antihistamines and cough medicines all impair reactions, and driving when you can no longer control the car safely is an offence, prescription or not.

questions.text: Which statements about the points system in the Fahreignungsregister ("points in Flensburg") are correct?

options.text: A single violation is worth one, two or three points, depending on how serious it is
At four or five points you receive a written Ermahnung; at six or seven a written Verwarnung
All entries are automatically deleted after exactly two years, whatever the violation was

questions.explanation: One point is given for ordinary road-safety offences, two for particularly serious offences (typically those that also bring a driving ban) and for traffic crimes without licence withdrawal, and three for traffic crimes in which the court withdraws the licence or orders an isolated bar on re-applying (Sperre). The ladder of measures is fixed: admonition at 4–5 points, warning at 6–7, withdrawal at 8. Deletion periods differ by entry: two years and six months for 1-point entries, five years for 2-point entries and ten years for 3-point entries — each entry ages on its own clock, so there is no single reset date.

questions.text: It is late, you are on the Berlin city motorway and your eyelids are getting heavy. What is correct?

options.text: Microsleep can strike without warning and last several seconds, during which you effectively drive with your eyes shut
Strong emotions such as rage after an argument also reduce your fitness to drive, because they narrow attention and increase risk-taking
A strong coffee and loud music reliably cancel out serious tiredness

questions.explanation: Microsleep gives no reliable warning, and a few seconds at motorway speed means dozens of metres travelled blind. Caffeine, cold air and music postpone the feeling of tiredness without restoring your reactions — the only real remedy is to leave the road and sleep for 15 to 20 minutes, and to plan a break roughly every two hours on long trips. Emotional states count as fitness problems too: anger, grief or panic narrow your attention exactly when you need it wide.

questions.text: What is the highest maximum authorised mass (zulässige Gesamtmasse), in kilograms, that a single vehicle may have for you to drive it on a plain class B licence?
questions.explanation: Class B stops at 3,500 kg maximum authorised mass — the fully loaded figure printed in the vehicle registration document, not the empty weight. Key number B96 raises the limit for a car-plus-trailer combination to 4,250 kg, but the towing car itself still has to stay within class B.

questions.text: How many points in the Fahreignungsregister mean that your driving licence must be withdrawn?
questions.explanation: At eight points the authority has no choice: the licence is withdrawn. You may apply for a new one at the earliest six months later, and normally only after a positive medical-psychological assessment (MPU). The voluntary driver fitness seminar that removes one point is only available while you are on 1 to 5 points, and only once every five years — so you cannot use it to climb back down from eight.

questions.text: You are driving at 90 km/h and have a microsleep (Sekundenschlaf) lasting 2 seconds. How many metres do you travel with your eyes effectively closed?
questions.explanation: Convert speed to metres per second by dividing by 3.6: 90 ÷ 3.6 = 25 m/s. Two seconds therefore means 2 × 25 = 50 metres — about the length of a Berlin tram plus a bus, covered completely blind. That is why tiredness is treated as seriously as alcohol: no braking, no steering, no reaction at all.
